# 20260920-0639-container-management Declared containers, generated by Quadlet, observed through podman

- **status**: completed
- **createdAt**: 2026-09-20 06:39
- **approvedAt**: 2026-09-20 06:52
- **relatedTask**: 20260920-0640-container-management

## Context

Device testing asked for a container management page: add, remove, stop and
edit containers. The device has none of it.

What exists today is one switch. `container.enabled` is a bool in the settings
tree, and `ContainerReconciler` (`crates/micad/src/reconciler/container.rs`)
does exactly one thing with it: it brings `etc-containers-systemd.mount` up or
down and issues a `daemon-reload`, so `/etc/containers/systemd` -- Quadlet's
search directory, bound from STATE -- exists only while containers are enabled.
Nothing writes a unit into it. The console's container page is a disabled form
for a registry credential the device has no field for.

Three facts from `micaoss/mica-podman` shape everything below:

- **The engine is daemonless.** `podman run` forks `conmon`, which execs
  `crun`, and nothing stays resident. mica-podman deliberately ships no podman
  unit at all: no `podman.socket`, no service. There is no API socket to talk
  to, and adding one would be a new resident root daemon on an appliance that
  does not have one.
- **Quadlet is the supported way in.** The package ships `quadlet`, the systemd
  generator that turns a `.container` file into a `.service`, and mica-core
  already owns the directory it reads.
- **Container storage is `/mica/containers`** on DATA, declared by
  mica-podman's `/etc/containers` configuration.

The architectural constraint that decides the shape: **micad never supervises
processes.** It renders configuration and asks systemd to start, stop, restart
or reload units (`docs/architecture.md` §2). A management surface that called
`podman run` would be micad supervising a process, and nothing would bring the
container back after a reboot.

The user chose: Quadlet units as the write path, podman **read-only** for
observation, so what the console shows is the engine's own answer rather than a
restatement of the file micad wrote.

## Proposal

### 1. Containers are declared settings, not uploaded files

A new `container.units` map in the settings tree, one entry per container,
carried by the existing `container.json` document (schema bump, additive).

```rust
/// One container this device runs, as the fields a `.container` unit needs.
pub struct ContainerUnit {
    pub image: String,
    #[serde(default)] pub command: Vec<String>,
    #[serde(default)] pub environment: BTreeMap<String, String>,
    #[serde(default)] pub publish: Vec<PublishedPort>,   // host:container/proto
    #[serde(default)] pub volumes: Vec<VolumeMount>,     // host path -> container path, ro flag
    #[serde(default)] pub restart: RestartPolicy,        // no | on-failure | always
    #[serde(default)] pub auto_start: bool,              // WantedBy=multi-user.target
}
```

`deny_unknown_fields`, like every other document. The subset is deliberately
small: it is what "add a container" needs, and a field nobody asked for is a
field the renderer has to keep honest forever.

Validation, total and before anything is written:

- the entry name is a systemd unit name fragment and is unique;
- the image reference parses and is not empty;
- a published host port is not claimed twice across the map;
- **a volume's host path is under `/mica/`**. A bind of `/` or `/etc` from a
  container is root on the device; the settings file stays writable without
  apid, so this bound is stated where every other relational rule is.

### 2. The reconciler renders `.container` files

`ContainerReconciler` gains a render-compare-sweep pass over
`/etc/containers/systemd`, the same discipline the network reconciler follows:

- render each entry to `50-mica-<name>.container` (a deterministic function of
  the entry), compare against what is on disk, write only on difference;
- sweep every `50-mica-` file the pass did not write;
- `daemon-reload` when anything changed, so Quadlet regenerates;
- bring each unit to its declared state through the existing `UnitControl`,
  runtime-scoped enablement as everywhere else.

**Fail closed when the switch is off**: with `container.enabled` false the
mount is not up, `/etc/containers/systemd` is not writable, and the reconciler
writes nothing and reports `disabled` rather than erroring.

### 3. podman answers what is actually running, read-only

A new observer, `crates/micad/src/containers.rs`, in the shape
`deployment.rs` already uses for `mica-deploy`: run the binary with bounded
time and bounded output, parse JSON, never shell out to anything else.

| Call | For |
| --- | --- |
| `podman ps --all --format json` | the runtime list: state, started-at, ports, image id |
| `podman images --format json` | what is on disk, for the image column and for "is this pulled" |
| `podman inspect <name> --format json` | one container, only when the detail page asks |

Read-only, exactly as decided: **no `podman run`, no `podman rm`, no
`podman pull`**. Starting a Quadlet unit pulls the image if it has to; that
keeps the one writer the unit file and its service.

It is a trait with an "unavailable" default, like every other observer, so a
dry-run daemon and every test that does not want podman never reach the host.

### 4. D-Bus and HTTP

New `com.mica.micad1` members (additive, so the interface name stands):

| Member | Answers |
| --- | --- |
| `GetContainers` | the declared map joined with podman's list, each side named |
| `StartContainer`, `StopContainer`, `RestartContainer` | systemd verbs on the generated `<name>.service`, never podman |

Containers are written like every other subtree, through `SetSettings` on
`container.units`, so one write is one commit and one apply task.

apid gains the resource routes:

```
GET    /api/v1/containers              declared + observed, not merged
PUT    /api/v1/containers/{name}       declare or replace one, whole entry
DELETE /api/v1/containers/{name}       remove one, re-validating the rest
POST   /api/v1/containers/{name}/start | /stop | /restart
```

POST-only actions, for the reason the power actions are POST-only. The
OpenAPI document is regenerated and committed.

### 5. The console

The Services → Containers page becomes a real page: the list (name, image,
unit state, published ports, image present), an add/edit dialog over the typed
entry, start/stop/restart, and a delete confirmation that says a removed
container's volumes under `/mica/` are not deleted with it.

### 6. Order of work

1. Settings model, validation, `container.json` schema bump, tests.
2. Reconciler render/compare/sweep, unit state, tests.
3. podman observer + `GetContainers` + the three unit actions, bus tests.
4. apid routes, OpenAPI, tests.
5. Console page, tests.
6. `docs/design/micad.md`, `docs/design/apid.md`, `docs/architecture.md`,
   changelog, and the `micad` / `mica-apid` producer version bumps.

## Risks

- **A document schema bump.** `container.json` gains a key, additive, so a v7
  tree and its predecessor differ by the version integer alone and an A/B
  rollback survives it -- the same argument the network `kind` bump made.
- **Host paths are root.** The `/mica/` bound above is the whole defence; it
  has to be in the model's validator and not only in apid, because the file is
  writable without apid.
- **Two packages move.** `micad` and `mica-apid` both change, so both producer
  versions bump and both inputs hashes move. Nothing else is touched.
- **podman absent.** On an image without the engine, or in dry run, the
  observer answers "unavailable" and the page says so rather than showing an
  empty list that reads as "no containers".
- **Unit name collisions.** A declared entry named after a system unit would
  have Quadlet generate a `<name>.service` that shadows nothing but confuses
  everything; the validator refuses names outside a `mica-` safe set or
  requires the rendered unit to carry the `50-mica-` prefix in its file name
  (decided in step 1, recorded there).
- **Reset tiers.** The `application-data` tier is documented as clearing
  operator applications and their data; declared containers are operator
  applications, so `reset.rs` has to clear `container.units` with them. Missing
  that would leave a factory-reset device still running someone's workload.

## Scope

Five crates' worth of change in one repository: `micad-settings` (model,
document, validation), `micad` (reconciler, observer, bus), `mica-apid`
(routes, OpenAPI), the console, and the docs. Roughly the size of the network
`kind` work. No new dependency: podman is invoked as a binary, and its JSON
goes through `serde_json`.

## Alternatives

- **Proxy podman directly** (the rejected B2). Every verb the engine has, for
  free, and a page that behaves like Portainer. Rejected: it makes micad a
  process supervisor, nothing survives a reboot unless podman's own restart
  policy is also configured, and either a resident socket appears on the device
  or apid starts running `podman` as root on request. It also puts two writers
  on the same containers -- the API and Quadlet -- with no arbiter.
- **Opaque `.container` file upload.** An operator uploads a unit file, apid
  stores it. Cheap, and it makes every Quadlet field available on day one.
  Rejected: nothing validates it, the reset tiers cannot reason about it, a
  provisioning document could not carry it, and the first unparsable file is a
  boot that does not converge.
- **A `podman`-backed read of state only, with no declaration** (a viewer, not
  a manager). Half the request, and the user asked for add/delete/edit.

## Annotations

- 2026-09-20: user chose Quadlet-as-writer with podman used read-only, so the
  running state shown is the engine's own answer. Container **logs** are not in
  this plan; the unit's journal is reachable through the existing failure
  evidence and a bounded log route can follow later if it is wanted.
